answer: Randomized Slot Allocation. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function draws an unpredictable inlet of registration slots from a fixed pool; agents must claim one within a short window, and a late or duplicate claim forfeits a per-attempt fee. Because the draw depends on future beacon output, attackers cannot precompute which epochs favor mass registration. Each fake identity therefore costs a repeated fee against a shale-thin success probability, making farming a relic of predictable timing.
